page.layout: One page of text, single column, with a heading block at top; faint show-through from the reverse page in the upper area; a library stamp and ink stamps over the left margin and lower centre (not printed text). Top: running head in small capitals (faint, partly legible), then a centred heading in large capitals and a smaller-capitals subheading; then the body paragraph beginning with an enlarged initial letter. No marginal notes.

main_text.head: LECTORI DE MENDIS Typographicis.
main_text.p: AMice Lector, cum percurrere ea quæ esfent edita propter occupationes non vacarit, rogamus petimusque, vt ingenue ac candide mendas per te typographicas emendes, quas haud magni momenti fore speramus.

page.notes: The running head at the top is faint and only partly legible; its reading is approximate. The initial "A" is a large woodcut-style letter joined to "Mice" and is transcribed as "AMice". The line "candide" is partly obscured by a stamp; "candide" is a likely reading and is marked as read from context. The text beneath the body is show-through from the reverse side and is omitted. The ink stamps and the "814,000" oval mark are not printed text and are omitted.
